validation_scope: Offline public-selection and clean-install tests plus specialist regression suites; live fresh-host acceptance outcomes and limitations are recorded separately in the review record.
changes: Creation recovery: the Sourcify request carries the deployment record (transaction hash, block, deployer) and supplies the creation transaction when the explorer's address page fails or names none (creation.tx_source and a printed creation: summary line record which source answered; a conflict between the two is printed and recorded, never resolved silently; the lane briefs name the deployer when only Sourcify answered); a transient failure of the explorer address page (server_error, timeout, throttled) gets one more charged attempt after a two-second pause on top of the fetcher's own quick retry, never on a 404, an access denial or a run whose every capture got no response. Motivated by two live PONS runs where a Blockscout 500 and then a timeout lost the creation receipt, the launch-window scan and the custodian probe.

start runs its recommended queue itself after charging the lanes (positions for GoPlus-listed unread LP ids, the bounded IncreaseLiquidity scans with their printed positions chained, unprobed listed sells) under the session's remaining seconds and requests, sharing one preset executor with `collect`; facts.presets_run and the preset-run summary lines record each outcome and only deferred rows stay in recommended_presets (a Codex STONK run stalled at a checkpoint when its host approval review treated a recommended preset as a new paid action). Phase 4 lists position custodians first, so a receipt-heavy run never pushes one past the ten-actor cap (a live PONS run lost its locker getters that way); the queue re-offers listed position ids a six-id row left unread and never an id already read.

GoPlus token security captured in discovery (keyless; doc-goplus-token-security): listed holders and LP holders with contract and lock flags and LP position ids, counts and control checks; facts.goplus carries the claims with pipeline cross-checks (LP holders verified by position ids the pipeline read, holders by the balance sample); unread listed LP position ids lead the recommended presets; the pipeline note states the enumeration in the custody finding and the checks as corroboration on token controls and holder distribution. Motivated by the PONS custody row: GoPlus enumerates the canonical pool's LP holders (locker 59.4%, next 9.6%, none locked) where a log scan could only sample. Unread listed LP position ids are ranked largest share first, in-range before out-of-range, a zero-amount position never queued; positions read by a later positions preset are merged into the pipeline note's cross-check on recompose (matched through the imported row's provenance alias, which carries no collection prefix), so the custody finding names them as verified.

Custody reads move into the pipeline: every probed owner's Safe module page (getModulesPaginated from the sentinel, with a truncation flag) and guard slot are read and decoded (owners[*].safe_modules, safe_modules_truncated, safe_guard, safe_guard_read); a position custodian with code, matched by address even when a receipt or the token names it first, answers its withdrawal getters (owner, beneficiary, unlock/lock/release times, token, nft, positionManager, paused) in a second bounded collection phase4b (actors[*].role position_custodian with getters and reverted; EOA owners are position_owner_without_code); log rows decode IncreaseLiquidity token ids; facts.json and recommended-presets.json carry recommended_presets derived from the facts (a launch-window IncreaseLiquidity log scan from the creation block, then a recent window only when disjoint, when identified positions cover under 80% of active liquidity; then positions for the printed ids) and the start summary prints them; work-plan.json keeps the validator's shape. Motivated by the PONS run whose coordinator spent presets on the dead address and never on the Safe or the locker.

Indexer-listed sale candidates: discovery captures GeckoTerminal's recent trades for the canonical pool (registry geckoterminal network ids) and fills the remaining sale-candidate slots with listed sells (one slot always goes to the most recent listed sell when the explorer named two, since a wallet-to-pool transfer can be a liquidity add); facts.indexed carries indexed_trades_captured and indexed_sells, and recommended_presets names a receipts preset for unprobed listed sells when no sale verified. The receipt, never the listing, establishes the sale.

Start names a whole-host network denial: when every web discovery host and the RPC chain check fail before any response, start-failed.json carries category network_unavailable with transport_category and the discovery statuses, and its next step asks for network permission for the start command itself before the identical in-place restart; a single-host transport failure keeps its exact category. Motivated by the Solana sandbox-denial live failure; synthetic regression coverage plus a sandbox-exec reproduction on macOS.

Chain-specific built-in public RPC defaults for seven registered mainnets, explicit credential-free public selection, unchanged configured-provider authorization gates, and target-derived selection for presets and low-level collections. Separate per-command paid flags from repeat consent; exercise clean link/copy installation and report delivery.

Publication hardening: anonymous EVM web captures reject private destinations and connected peers, validate redirects, and ignore environment proxies. Claude uses ordinary host tool permissions without shipped auto-allow wildcards.

Production review: bounded retry/redirect/restart accounting, exact same-pool sale matching, missing-data and authority wording, and reliable internal checkpoints. No added research steps, tool calls or agent turns.

Exact unique-address holder aggregates from atomic RPC balances, runtime-shape classification and explicit sample exclusions; existing delivery response preserves coverage beyond optional summary signals. No added network requests, tool calls or agent turns.

Browser-like User-Agent on the RPC transport and the web fetcher: Cloudflare fronts (public Robinhood RPC, Blockscout) reject generic and Chrome-without-hints agents with 403; verified answered with a Safari-style agent
Discovery captures explorer counters, top-50 holders and recent transfers; sale candidates are transfers into a pool from non-contract wallets

Pipeline reads counter-asset reserves per pool, the ten largest indexed holders' balances with a code check each, up to two sale receipts at their own pins (decoded: seller, pool, amount, counter received, Swap events), and the launch signer's explorer transactions and token transfers

facts.json gains sales, top_holders, creator_activity, maturity (age from the creation pin, indexed counts and market aggregates labeled by source) and indexed capture counts; receipts carry a role (creation, sale_candidate) and the creation receipt sets creation.signer/factory/block
pipeline_note.py writes and composes notes/pipeline.json: deterministic factual findings from facts (no signal); start and every collect regenerate it
compose accepts a coordinator `signals` block that assigns topic/signal to existing findings under the same Good/Bad/Unverified rules; the scaffold pre-lists every pipeline finding in it
web fetcher retries transient failures once; default start budget 300 requests
Previous 3.3.0 changes retained: reverted classification, one transient RPC retry, structured start diagnostics with restart, briefs as files, compose execution/coverage repairs, scaffold
Engine snapshots include pipeline_note.py; 3.0.0-3.3.0 collections remain loadable
